salt__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Salt","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Salt is used to enhance flavor and preserve food but can contribute to high sodium intake. Excessive sodium is linked to high blood pressure and cardiovascular risk.","details":"In typical processed foods, salt is a major source of dietary sodium, and frequent consumption can push intake above recommended daily limits. People with hypertension, kidney disease, or heart conditions need to be especially cautious about cumulative sodium from multiple foods. In normal amounts within a generally balanced diet, salt is tolerated well by most healthy individuals, but processed products often contain higher levels than home-cooked foods.","category":"Flavoring and preservative"}

peanut butter (ground peanuts)__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Peanut Butter (ground Peanuts)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Peanut butter made from ground peanuts is an energy-dense source of healthy fats, protein, and some fiber. It is a common allergen but safe for the general population when consumed in moderation.","details":"Ground peanuts provide mostly unsaturated fats, plant protein, vitamin E, magnesium, and other micronutrients that can support heart health when part of a balanced diet. For most people, plain peanut butter without added sugar, hydrogenated oils, or excessive salt is a relatively wholesome ingredient, though it is calorie-dense and can contribute to weight gain if overeaten. The major health concern is for individuals with peanut allergy, but for those without allergies it is considered safe.","category":"Nut and seed products"}

corn grits__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Corn Grits","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Corn grits are a processed form of corn used as a grain or cereal base. They mainly provide carbohydrates with some fiber, vitamins, and minerals depending on the level of refining and enrichment.","details":"As a staple carbohydrate source, corn grits can be part of a balanced diet, especially when paired with protein, healthy fats, and vegetables. More refined grits may be lower in fiber and nutrients than whole-grain corn products, but they do not typically pose specific health risks on their own. Sodium or unhealthy fats would only be a concern if added during processing or preparation, not from the corn grits themselves.","category":"Grain and cereal products"}

sunflower oil__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Sunflower Oil","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Sunflower oil is a vegetable oil rich in unsaturated fats, commonly used for cooking and in processed foods. In moderate amounts, it can be part of a healthy diet, though it is calorie-dense.","details":"High-oleic sunflower oil varieties are generally more stable for cooking and provide mostly monounsaturated fats, which are considered heart-healthier. Standard sunflower oil is high in omega-6 polyunsaturated fats, which may contribute to an imbalanced omega-6 to omega-3 ratio if consumed in large amounts alongside a diet already rich in seed oils. Overall, when used in reasonable quantities and within a balanced dietary pattern, sunflower oil is considered safe for the general population.","category":"Fats and oils"}

wheat flour__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Wheat Flour","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Refined or whole milled wheat used as a base carbohydrate and structural ingredient in many foods. It is a common allergen but generally safe for the non-allergic population.","details":"Wheat flour primarily provides starch and some protein (including gluten), contributing calories and texture but relatively few micronutrients if refined. For most people it is safe, though those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity must avoid it, and excessive intake of refined wheat products can contribute to high glycemic load in the diet. Whole wheat flour is nutritionally superior to refined versions due to higher fiber, vitamins, and minerals.","category":"Grain / carbohydrate source"}

sugar__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Sugar","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Simple carbohydrate (usually sucrose) used as a sweetener and preservative. Safe in small amounts but potentially harmful when consumed in excess.","details":"High intake of added sugar is associated with increased risk of weight gain, type 2 diabetes, dental cavities, and cardiovascular disease. It offers calories without significant vitamins, minerals, or fiber, so products listing sugar high in the ingredients may contribute to a high added-sugar diet. Moderation and balancing with minimally processed, nutrient-dense foods is advisable.","category":"Sweetener / added sugar"}

pasteurized milk__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Pasteurized Milk","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Pasteurized milk is heat-treated cow’s milk used as a primary base in many dairy products. It is generally safe for the general population but is a common allergen for people with milk allergy or lactose intolerance.","details":"Pasteurization reduces harmful bacteria while preserving most of the nutritional value, including protein, calcium, and vitamins. For individuals without milk allergy or lactose intolerance, it is considered safe and nutritionally beneficial. Those with dairy sensitivities may experience digestive or allergic symptoms, but this does not increase risk for the general population.","category":"Dairy ingredient"}

cheese cultures__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Cheese Cultures","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Cheese cultures are beneficial bacteria used to ferment milk and develop flavor and texture in cheese. They are generally recognized as safe for most people.","details":"These cultures typically include strains of lactic acid bacteria that help acidify milk, improve shelf life, and create characteristic cheese flavors. They are a normal part of traditional cheese-making and do not usually pose health concerns for the general population. People with specific sensitivities to certain microbes rarely may need to be cautious, but this is uncommon.","category":"Fermentation culture"}

enzymes__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Enzymes","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Enzymes in cheese-making are proteins (such as rennet) that help coagulate milk and form curds. They are used in very small amounts and are generally safe for most people.","details":"These enzymes may be animal-derived, microbial, or fermentation-produced and are widely used in modern dairy processing. While some individuals with strict dietary preferences (for example, vegetarian or certain religious diets) may care about the source, typical health risk for the general population is low. Regulatory agencies generally recognize standard cheese-making enzymes as safe at the levels used.","category":"Processing aid / enzyme"}

processed honey__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Processed Honey","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Processed honey is honey that has been heated and filtered to improve shelf life and clarity. It is generally safe for most people when consumed in moderation but is high in sugar.","details":"Processing typically involves pasteurization (heating) and fine filtration, which can reduce beneficial enzymes and trace nutrients compared to raw honey while improving texture and stability. The main health concern is its high content of simple sugars, which can contribute to excess calorie intake, blood sugar spikes, and dental issues if overconsumed. It is not suitable for infants under one year due to the risk of infant botulism.","category":"Sweetener"}

tomato paste__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Tomato Paste","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Tomato paste is a concentrated form of cooked tomatoes used as a flavor base and thickener. It is generally considered safe and can be a source of vitamins and antioxidants like lycopene.","details":"It is made by cooking tomatoes for a long time to reduce water content, then straining out skins and seeds to form a thick paste. Tomato paste can provide vitamin C, potassium, and carotenoid antioxidants, especially lycopene, which may support heart health. Any health concerns usually come from added salt or other additives in some commercial products, not from the tomato paste itself.","category":"Vegetable concentrate"}

fermented milk__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Fermented Milk","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Fermented milk is milk that has been cultured with beneficial bacteria, similar to yogurt or kefir. It is generally safe for most people and may support gut health through probiotics.","details":"During fermentation, bacteria convert some of the lactose (milk sugar) into lactic acid, which can make the product easier to digest for some lactose-sensitive individuals. Fermented milk products can provide protein, calcium, and live cultures that may help maintain a healthy gut microbiome. As a dairy product, it is a common allergen for people with milk allergy, but for the general population it is considered low risk when consumed in normal amounts.","category":"Dairy product"}

tomato powder__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Tomato Powder","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Tomato powder is a dehydrated, ground form of tomatoes used for flavor and color. It is generally safe and nutrient-rich for most people.","details":"Tomato powder concentrates natural tomato components, including vitamins, minerals, fiber, and antioxidants such as lycopene. Potential concerns are mainly for individuals with tomato allergy, histamine intolerance, or acid-sensitive reflux, but for the general population it is considered a wholesome, low-risk ingredient. It is not an artificial additive and typically does not introduce significant processing-related hazards.","category":"Dried vegetable ingredient"}

dried onion__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Dried Onion","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Dried onion is a dehydrated form of onion used as a seasoning. It is generally safe for most people and contributes flavor and some phytonutrients.","details":"Drying removes water while preserving onion’s sulfur compounds and some antioxidants that may offer minor health benefits. The main issues are for people with onion or allium allergies or those sensitive to FODMAPs, who may experience digestive discomfort, but this does not affect the general population risk rating. It is a simple dried vegetable ingredient rather than an artificial additive.","category":"Dried vegetable ingredient"}

glucose__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Glucose","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Glucose is a simple sugar used as a sweetener and energy source. It is safe in small to moderate amounts but can contribute to metabolic issues when consumed in excess.","details":"As a rapidly absorbed carbohydrate, glucose can cause quick rises in blood sugar and insulin, which is a concern for people with diabetes, insulin resistance, or metabolic syndrome. High intake of added sugars, including glucose, is associated with increased risk of weight gain, cardiovascular disease, and dental caries. In normal dietary amounts within an overall balanced diet, it is generally safe, but its role as an added sugar raises its risk level compared with whole-food ingredients.","category":"Sugar / sweetener"}

palm oil__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Palm Oil","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Palm oil is a widely used vegetable oil that is high in saturated fat, which can negatively affect heart health when consumed in excess. Its health impact depends strongly on overall diet quality and how much is eaten.","details":"Palm oil raises LDL (“bad”) cholesterol less than some animal fats but more than many unsaturated vegetable oils, so frequent or heavy use can contribute to cardiovascular risk over time. Refined palm oil used in processed foods is often highly processed and typically appears in products that are also high in sugar, salt, or other less healthy ingredients. It does not pose a common allergen risk, but from a nutritional standpoint it is best used in moderation and balanced with healthier unsaturated fats.","category":"Vegetable oil / fat source"}

canola oil__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Canola Oil","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Canola oil is a vegetable oil relatively high in unsaturated fats and low in saturated fat, generally considered a heart-friendlier option compared to many other cooking fats. It is commonly used in cooking and in processed foods.","details":"Canola oil contains monounsaturated fats and some omega-3 fatty acids, which can support cardiovascular health when it replaces saturated fats. Potential concerns relate mainly to refinement and frequent use of highly processed forms in packaged foods, not to acute toxicity. For most people, moderate use of canola oil within a balanced diet is considered low risk.","category":"Vegetable oil / fat source"}

soy lecithin__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Soy Lecithin","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Soy lecithin is an emulsifier derived from soy that helps blend fats and water in foods. It is generally recognized as safe and used in very small amounts in many processed products.","details":"Although it comes from soy, a common allergen, highly refined soy lecithin contains only trace protein and usually does not trigger reactions in most people with soy allergy, though sensitive individuals should still be cautious. Typical intake levels from foods are low, and there is no strong evidence of harm for the general population. It mainly indicates the product is processed but, by itself, is considered a low-risk additive.","category":"Emulsifier / processing aid"}

corn starch__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Corn Starch","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Corn starch is a refined carbohydrate used mainly as a thickener and texturizer in foods. It is generally safe for most people when consumed in typical culinary amounts.","details":"Corn starch is produced by milling and processing corn to isolate the starchy portion, resulting in a nearly pure carbohydrate with minimal protein, fat, or micronutrients. It is easily digestible and rapidly raises blood glucose, so very high intakes may be less ideal for people managing blood sugar. In normal food uses as a thickener or coating, it does not present notable health risks for the general population.","category":"Thickener / Refined carbohydrate"}

spices__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Spices","riskLevel":"low","summary":"“Spices” is a generic term that usually refers to a blend of dried plant seasonings used for flavor. It is generally safe, though sensitive individuals may react to specific spices within the blend.","details":"A spice blend can include ingredients such as black pepper, paprika, cumin, coriander, cloves, or others, depending on the product. Spices are typically used in small amounts and can provide beneficial phytochemicals and flavor without adding calories, sugar, or unhealthy fats. People with known sensitivities or reflux may need to monitor specific spices, but for most individuals, mixed spices pose minimal health risk.","category":"Flavoring / Spice blend"}

garlic__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Garlic","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Garlic is a culinary herb used for flavor that may offer some cardiovascular and immune-supportive properties. It is generally safe in food amounts for most people.","details":"Garlic contains sulfur compounds such as allicin that contribute to its characteristic odor and potential health benefits, including modest effects on blood lipids and antimicrobial activity. In typical food use, it poses little risk, though large amounts may cause digestive discomfort in some people or interact with blood-thinning medications. Overall, as a seasoning ingredient, garlic is considered a low-risk, flavorful addition to foods.","category":"Herb / Spice"}

monosodium glutamate__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Monosodium Glutamate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Monosodium glutamate (MSG) is a flavor enhancer that intensifies savory (umami) taste. It is considered safe for the general population at typical dietary intakes.","details":"Regulatory agencies such as the FDA and EFSA regard MSG as generally recognized as safe, and multiple studies have not confirmed consistent adverse effects in healthy people at normal consumption levels. Some individuals report transient symptoms like headache or flushing after large doses on an empty stomach, but this is not considered a general toxicity. The main nutritional concern is that MSG can contribute modestly to overall sodium intake, though usually less than table salt for the same flavor impact.","category":"Flavor enhancer / food additive"}

defatted soybean__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Defatted Soybean","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Defatted soybean is soy from which most of the oil has been removed, often used as a protein-rich ingredient. It is a common allergen but is safe for the general population without soy allergy.","details":"Removing the fat concentrates protein and some carbohydrates, making defatted soybean a common base for soy flour, textured vegetable protein, and other processed foods. It naturally contains soy proteins and small amounts of antinutritional factors (like trypsin inhibitors), which are largely reduced by heat processing. For people with soy allergy it can trigger reactions, but for others it is a normal, nutritionally useful ingredient.","category":"Plant protein / common allergen (soy)"}

yeast extract__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Yeast Extract","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Yeast extract is a flavoring ingredient derived from yeast cells that provides a strong savory (umami) taste. It is generally recognized as safe for most people when consumed in typical food amounts.","details":"Yeast extract naturally contains glutamates and nucleotides, which enhance savory flavor similarly to MSG, and is commonly used in soups, sauces, and snack foods. It can contribute to overall sodium intake and may be a concern for individuals who are highly sensitive to glutamates, but evidence for broad harm in the general population is limited. It also contains B vitamins and peptides, though the amounts in processed foods are usually small nutritionally.","category":"Flavor enhancer / food ingredient"}

onion extract__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Onion Extract","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Onion extract is a concentrated form of onion used for flavoring and potential antioxidant benefits. It is generally safe for most people when consumed in typical food amounts.","details":"This ingredient is usually produced by concentrating the flavors and active compounds from onions, providing a strong savory taste without whole onion pieces. It may cause digestive discomfort in people sensitive to FODMAPs or with irritable bowel syndrome, but this is not a concern for the general population. It does not typically present issues related to artificial additives, heavy metals, or vitamin toxicity.","category":"Natural flavoring / vegetable extract"}

soy sauce__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Soy Sauce","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Soy sauce is a fermented seasoning made mainly from soybeans, wheat, salt, and water, commonly used to add umami and saltiness. It is generally safe for most people but can be high in sodium and is a common allergen for those sensitive to soy or wheat.","details":"From a health perspective, the main concern with soy sauce is its very high sodium content, which can contribute to elevated blood pressure if consumed in large amounts or frequently. Traditional brewed soy sauce typically does not contain problematic artificial colors or sweeteners, though some commercial versions may add preservatives or flavor enhancers. For the general population without hypertension or sodium-sensitive conditions, it is safe when used in moderation.","category":"Condiment / fermented soy product"}

garlic extract__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Garlic Extract","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Garlic extract is a concentrated form of garlic used for flavor and potential health benefits such as antioxidant and cardiovascular support. It is generally safe in normal food quantities.","details":"This extract provides garlic’s characteristic flavor and some of its bioactive sulfur compounds without needing fresh garlic cloves. In sensitive individuals, large amounts may cause digestive upset or heartburn, but this is uncommon at typical seasoning levels. It is not associated with artificial additives, major toxicity, or heavy metal risks in standard food products.","category":"Natural flavoring / herbal extract"}

dried garlic__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Dried Garlic","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Dried garlic is a dehydrated form of garlic used as a seasoning and flavoring agent. It is generally safe and can offer some of the same beneficial compounds as fresh garlic.","details":"Dried garlic contains sulfur compounds that may support cardiovascular and immune health, though amounts in typical seasoning use are modest. Potential issues mainly involve digestive discomfort or heartburn in sensitive individuals when consumed in larger quantities. It is not a common allergen and does not typically pose a risk to the general population.","category":"Herb and spice"}

maltose__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Maltose","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Maltose is a simple carbohydrate (sugar) composed of two glucose units and is used as a sweetener or carbohydrate source. It contributes calories and can raise blood sugar levels.","details":"As a sugar, maltose can contribute to excess calorie intake and may promote weight gain and dental caries when consumed in large amounts, especially as part of a high-sugar diet. It can cause rapid increases in blood glucose, which may be a concern for people with insulin resistance or diabetes. For most healthy individuals, occasional intake in moderate amounts is not harmful, but frequent high intake of added sugars is linked to metabolic and cardiovascular risks.","category":"Sugar and sweetener"}

whey powder__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Whey Powder","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Whey powder is a dairy-derived protein and lactose source commonly used in food products and supplements. It is a common milk allergen but is safe for the general population without milk allergy or lactose intolerance.","details":"Whey powder provides high-quality protein and small amounts of minerals, and is widely used in protein powders, baked goods, and processed foods. In those with milk allergy or severe lactose intolerance it can trigger adverse reactions, but this concern is specific to those individuals, not the general population. For most people, moderate consumption is safe, though very high protein intake may strain kidney function in those with preexisting kidney disease.","category":"Dairy ingredient"}

citric acid__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Citric Acid","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Citric acid is a common food acid and preservative used to add tart flavor and improve shelf life. It is generally recognized as safe for most people when consumed in normal food amounts.","details":"Citric acid is naturally present in citrus fruits, but food-grade citric acid is usually produced by fermentation using microorganisms. It helps control acidity, preserve color, and inhibit microbial growth in many drinks and processed foods. A small subset of individuals may experience mouth or stomach irritation or sensitivity at high intakes, but this is uncommon at typical dietary levels.","category":"Acidulant and preservative"}

mono- and diglycerides__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Mono- And Diglycerides","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Mono- and diglycerides are emulsifiers used to blend water and fats and improve texture in processed foods. They can contain small amounts of trans fats and are a marker of higher processing.","details":"These compounds are derived from glycerol and fatty acids, often sourced from vegetable oils, and help stabilize products like baked goods, margarine, and ice cream. While they are permitted and widely used, they may introduce minor amounts of trans fats that do not have to be listed separately on labels in some regions. For people aiming to minimize ultra-processed ingredients and any avoidable trans fat exposure, frequent high intake of foods containing these emulsifiers may be less desirable.","category":"Emulsifier and texture enhancer"}

cocoa powder (processed with alkali)__fo.analysis: {"name":"Cocoa Powder (processed With Alkali)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Cocoa powder processed with alkali (Dutch-processed cocoa) is cocoa that has been treated to reduce acidity and create a milder flavor and darker color. It is generally safe for most people when consumed in typical food amounts.","details":"The alkalization process (Dutching) uses alkaline salts to neutralize cocoa’s natural acidity, which improves solubility and changes taste but can reduce some natural antioxidant content. Cocoa naturally contains caffeine and theobromine, so very large amounts could cause mild stimulant effects in sensitive individuals, but this is rarely an issue at typical dietary intakes. People managing reflux or caffeine sensitivity may want to watch total cocoa and chocolate consumption rather than this ingredient alone.","category":"Cocoa-based ingredient"}

sucrose fatty acid esters__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Sucrose Fatty Acid Esters","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Sucrose fatty acid esters are emulsifiers made from sucrose (sugar) and fatty acids, used to help mix oil and water in foods. They are generally considered safe at typical food use levels.","details":"These additives improve texture, stability, and mouthfeel in processed foods such as baked goods, confectionery, and beverages. Regulatory authorities like JECFA and the EU have established acceptable daily intakes, and toxicity studies show low concern at normal consumption levels, though very high intakes may cause mild digestive upset in some individuals. For most people, they do not pose a significant health risk when consumed as part of a balanced diet.","category":"Food additive – emulsifier"}

dextrose anhydrous (glucose)__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Dextrose Anhydrous (glucose)","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Dextrose anhydrous is a purified form of glucose, a simple sugar used as a sweetener and quick energy source. It is safe for most people but can contribute to excessive sugar intake if consumed in large amounts.","details":"As a rapidly absorbed carbohydrate, dextrose can quickly raise blood glucose and insulin levels, which is useful in some sports or medical contexts but undesirable when frequently consumed in sugary foods or drinks. High intake of added sugars is associated with increased risk of weight gain, dental cavities, insulin resistance, and metabolic diseases over time. Individuals with diabetes or impaired glucose tolerance should be particularly cautious with ingredients like dextrose.","category":"Sweetener – simple sugar"}

banana__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Banana","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Banana is a whole fruit that provides natural sugars, fiber, potassium, vitamin B6, and other nutrients. It is considered safe and healthful for the general population when eaten in normal amounts.","details":"The natural sugars in banana are balanced by fiber and micronutrients, making it a more nutritious carbohydrate source than refined sugars. Bananas can support heart and muscle function due to their potassium content, and they are generally easy to digest. Only specific groups, such as people with severe kidney disease or those on potassium-restricted diets, may need to moderate high banana intake under medical guidance.","category":"Whole food – fruit"}

onion flake__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Onion Flake","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Onion flake is dehydrated onion used for flavoring. It is generally safe and can provide some of the same beneficial compounds as fresh onion.","details":"Dehydrated onion concentrates flavor and is commonly used in seasoning blends, soups, and snacks. It contains trace amounts of antioxidants and sulfur compounds, though in smaller quantities than fresh onion. The main concern is for individuals with specific onion or allium sensitivity, but for the general population it is considered low risk.","category":"Herb and spice"}

natural flavor__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Natural Flavor","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Natural flavor is a broad term for flavoring substances derived from plant or animal sources. Its vague labeling can be an issue for people with sensitivities or those avoiding certain animal-derived ingredients.","details":"Although regulated, the term \"natural flavor\" can cover complex mixtures, including solvents or carriers, and manufacturers do not have to specify the exact source on the label. For most people, these ingredients are tolerated without obvious harm, but they may occasionally trigger reactions in sensitive individuals or those with specific allergies or dietary restrictions. The lack of transparency and potential for undisclosed allergens or animal-derived components justifies a moderate caution level.","category":"Flavoring agent"}

garlic flake__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Garlic Flake","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Garlic flakes are simply dehydrated pieces of garlic used for flavoring foods. They are generally safe for most people when eaten in normal culinary amounts.","details":"Garlic contains sulfur compounds that can support flavor and may have some health benefits, but in food products the primary role is taste. Large amounts may cause digestive discomfort, heartburn, or bad breath in sensitive individuals, but this is not a concern at typical usage levels. There are no major toxicity concerns for the general population.","category":"Herb and spice"}

paprika color__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Paprika Color","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Paprika color is a natural coloring made from paprika peppers, used to give foods a red to orange hue. It is generally considered safe as a natural colorant.","details":"This color is derived from carotenoid pigments (like capsanthin and capsorubin) extracted from paprika. Regulatory agencies typically regard it as safe when used within approved limits, and it is less concerning than many synthetic dyes. Rarely, people sensitive to peppers may experience mild reactions, but this is uncommon at normal food levels.","category":"Natural color additive"}

disodium inosinate__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Disodium Inosinate","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Disodium inosinate is a flavor enhancer often used with MSG to boost savory (umami) taste. It is generally safe at approved levels but can indicate a highly processed, strongly flavored product.","details":"This additive is usually present in very small amounts and is considered non-toxic at typical intake levels. However, it is frequently combined with monosodium glutamate (MSG) and disodium guanylate, which some individuals report sensitivity to (headache or flushing), though strong scientific evidence of harm to the general population is limited. Its presence may suggest high flavor enhancement and sometimes higher sodium content in the overall product.","category":"Flavor enhancer"}

whole milk powder__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Whole Milk Powder","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Dehydrated whole cow’s milk that retains milk fat, protein, lactose, and minerals. Generally safe for most people but is a common allergen for those with milk allergy or lactose intolerance.","details":"Whole milk powder is produced by removing water from pasteurized whole milk, concentrating its nutrients and calories, including saturated fat. For the general population it is considered safe and a good source of protein and calcium, though high intake can contribute to higher saturated fat and calorie consumption. Individuals with milk allergy or severe lactose intolerance should avoid it, but this does not increase risk for the general population.","category":"Dairy ingredient"}

skim milk powder__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Skim Milk Powder","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Dehydrated nonfat cow’s milk containing milk proteins, lactose, and minerals but little to no fat. Safe for most people, though it is still a common milk allergen.","details":"Skim milk powder is made by removing most of the fat from milk and then drying it, leaving a concentrated source of milk proteins (including casein and whey), lactose, and micronutrients such as calcium. It is widely used in foods to add protein, texture, and dairy flavor with less fat than whole milk powder. As with all milk ingredients, it can trigger reactions in people with milk allergy or lactose intolerance, but this does not pose extra risk for the general population.","category":"Dairy ingredient"}

caramel color__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Caramel Color","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"A widely used brown food color created by heating carbohydrates, sometimes with acids, alkalis, or salts. Generally recognized as safe, but certain types can contain trace levels of 4-MEI, a processing byproduct linked to potential cancer risk at high exposures in animals.","details":"Caramel color is used to give foods and drinks a brown hue and is produced by controlled heating of sugars; Class III and IV caramel colors may form 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI) during processing. Regulatory agencies consider typical dietary exposure safe, but very high or chronic intake from many dark-colored sodas and processed foods could modestly increase long-term risk, so limiting heavily colored soft drinks and ultra-processed foods is prudent. People sensitive to processed additives or trying to minimize potential carcinogen exposure may choose to moderate intake, though occasional consumption is unlikely to be harmful.","category":"Color additive"}

tomato extract__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Tomato Extract","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Tomato extract is a concentrated form of tomato, often used for flavor, color, and as a source of antioxidants like lycopene. It is generally safe for most people when consumed in typical food amounts.","details":"This ingredient is typically produced by concentrating tomatoes to retain beneficial compounds such as lycopene, vitamins, and organic acids. Potential concerns are minor and mainly related to individual sensitivities to nightshades or acid reflux in people sensitive to acidic foods, rather than to additives or contaminants. It does not usually involve artificial colors, preservatives, or sweeteners by itself, though those would need to be checked elsewhere on the label.","category":"Natural plant extract / vegetable concentrate"}

soy protein hydrolysate__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Soy Protein Hydrolysate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Soy protein hydrolysate is soy protein that has been broken down into smaller peptides and amino acids to improve digestibility and solubility. It is generally safe for the general population, though soy is a common allergen.","details":"This ingredient is created by enzymatically or chemically hydrolyzing soy protein, which can slightly increase its free glutamate content and savory (umami) taste but is not the same as adding pure MSG. It is nutritionally rich in protein and often used in processed foods, meal replacements, and supplements, and any safety concerns mainly relate to people with soy allergy or intolerance rather than general toxicity. Typical manufacturing does not inherently introduce heavy metals or harmful additives, though overall sodium content of the finished product should still be checked on the full label.","category":"Protein ingredient / common allergen (soy)"}

apple puree__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Apple Puree","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Apple puree is a mashed or blended form of apples used for sweetness, texture, and natural flavor. It is generally considered safe and is a minimally processed fruit ingredient.","details":"This ingredient provides natural sugars, fiber, and phytonutrients from apples, and typically does not involve artificial colors, preservatives, or sweeteners unless stated elsewhere on the label. Potential issues are limited to its sugar content for those monitoring blood sugar or overall calorie intake, rather than to additives or contaminants. In normal food amounts, it is not associated with significant toxicity or long-term health risks.","category":"Fruit ingredient / puree"}

natural and artificial flavors__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Natural And Artificial Flavors","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"A mixture of flavoring chemicals from natural and synthetic sources used to enhance taste. Generally recognized as safe, but the exact compounds are not disclosed to consumers.","details":"Natural and artificial flavors can contain dozens of individual chemicals, solvents, and carriers, and manufacturers are not required to list each component, which reduces transparency. Most people tolerate them well, but a small subset may experience sensitivity, headaches, or digestive discomfort from certain flavor compounds or solvents. For those trying to avoid ultra-processed ingredients or undisclosed additives, this ingredient can be considered less desirable.","category":"Flavoring additives"}

honey__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Honey","riskLevel":"low","summary":"A natural sweetener produced by bees that primarily contains sugars such as fructose and glucose. Safe for most people when used in moderation but should not be given to infants under one year old.","details":"Honey is a source of simple sugars and calories, contributing to increased blood sugar and energy intake when consumed in large amounts. It may contain trace nutrients and antioxidants, but nutritionally it functions mainly as a sugar. Due to the risk of infant botulism, honey should be strictly avoided for babies under 12 months, but this does not affect the general healthy adult population.","category":"Natural sweetener"}

dextrin__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Dextrin","riskLevel":"low","summary":"A group of carbohydrates produced from starch, often used as a thickener, fiber source, or processing aid. Generally recognized as safe and commonly found in processed foods and supplements.","details":"Dextrin is partially hydrolyzed starch, typically derived from corn, wheat, or other starch sources, and is used to improve texture, stability, or mouthfeel. Most people digest it easily, though in larger amounts it may cause gas or mild digestive discomfort in sensitive individuals due to fermentation in the gut. It does not pose significant health concerns at typical food-use levels.","category":"Carbohydrate additive / thickener"}

water__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Water","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Water is a common base ingredient used as a solvent in personal care products.","details":"It helps dissolve and distribute other ingredients and provides hydration to the product. In most formulations, water is safe for general use, with quality depending on purification standards used in manufacturing.","category":"Solvent / Base"}

glycerin__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Glycerin","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Glycerin is a humectant that attracts and retains moisture in the skin or hair.","details":"It helps improve skin hydration, softness, and barrier function by drawing water into the outer layers of the skin. Glycerin is generally well tolerated, though very high concentrations may feel sticky or slightly tacky on the skin in some formulations.","category":"Humectant / Moisturizing agent"}

isopropyl palmitate__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Isopropyl Palmitate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Isopropyl Palmitate is an emollient that makes products feel smooth and helps soften the skin.","details":"It is derived from isopropyl alcohol and palmitic acid and is used to improve spreadability and reduce a greasy feel in formulations. While generally considered safe, it can be comedogenic for some acne-prone individuals and may contribute to clogged pores in higher concentrations or occlusive formulas.","category":"Emollient / Texture enhancer"}

dimethicone__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Dimethicone","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Dimethicone is a silicone-based polymer used to create a smooth, silky feel and to form a protective barrier on skin or hair.","details":"It helps reduce water loss, improves slip, and can fill in fine lines or rough texture, making products feel more elegant. Dimethicone is generally considered safe and non-irritating for most people, though a small number may experience breakouts or feel it is too occlusive, especially on very acne-prone skin.","category":"Silicone emollient / skin protectant"}

butyrospermum parkii (shea) butter__pers.analysis: {"name":"Butyrospermum Parkii (shea) Butter","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Shea butter is a rich natural fat extracted from the nuts of the shea tree, widely used as a moisturizing and skin-softening ingredient.","details":"It contains fatty acids and vitamins that help support the skin barrier, reduce dryness, and improve skin flexibility. It is generally well tolerated, though extremely sensitive individuals or those with specific nut sensitivities should patch test, even though it is considered safe for the general population.","category":"Natural emollient / plant butter"}

butyrospermum parkii (shea) oil__persona.analysis: {"name":"Butyrospermum Parkii (shea) Oil","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Shea oil is the liquid oil fraction derived from shea butter, used as a lighter moisturizing and conditioning ingredient.","details":"It provides many of the same fatty acids and conditioning benefits as shea butter but with a lighter, more spreadable texture suitable for face, hair, and body products. It is generally safe and non-irritating, though, as with other nut-derived ingredients, patch testing is advisable for people with highly reactive or allergy-prone skin.","category":"Natural emollient / plant oil"}

disodium edta__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Disodium Edta","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Disodium EDTA is a chelating agent used to bind metal ions and improve product stability and performance. It is generally considered safe at the low concentrations used in personal care products.","details":"This ingredient helps prevent product spoilage and discoloration by binding metal ions that can catalyze degradation. It has low skin penetration and is not known to be a significant skin irritant at typical use levels, though very sensitive individuals may experience mild irritation. Environmental persistence is a concern, but in terms of human topical use it is regarded as low risk.","category":"Chelating agent / stabilizer"}

sodium hydroxide__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Sodium Hydroxide","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Sodium hydroxide is a strong base used in small amounts to adjust the pH of cosmetics and personal care products. At controlled low levels in finished products it is generally safe, but in higher concentrations it is highly irritating and caustic.","details":"In skincare and haircare, sodium hydroxide is typically present at very low concentrations only to fine-tune pH, where it rarely causes irritation for most users. However, in more concentrated forms (such as in some hair relaxers or undiluted raw material), it can cause severe burns and eye damage, which is why its use level and product pH are strictly regulated. For leave-on products formulated within normal cosmetic pH ranges, risk is mainly for those with very sensitive or compromised skin.","category":"pH adjuster / alkalizing agent"}

tocopheryl acetate__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Tocopheryl Acetate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Tocopheryl acetate is a stable form of vitamin E commonly used as an antioxidant and skin-conditioning ingredient. It is generally well tolerated and considered low risk for most people.","details":"This ingredient helps protect both the product and the skin from oxidative damage and supports the skin barrier. While rare cases of contact allergy or irritation have been reported, overall sensitization rates are low, and it is widely used in cosmetics, moisturizers, and anti-aging products. Its safety profile is favorable at typical cosmetic concentrations, including in leave-on applications.","category":"Antioxidant / skin-conditioning agent"}

palmitic acid__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Palmitic Acid","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Palmitic acid is a fatty acid used as an emollient, thickener, and surfactant in personal care products. It is generally considered safe for most skin types.","details":"This ingredient is commonly derived from palm oil or other vegetable and animal fats and helps stabilize formulations while giving creams and soaps a richer texture. It can occasionally contribute to clogged pores in very acne-prone or oily skin, but it is not linked to major systemic health concerns such as endocrine disruption or carcinogenicity. Palmitic acid is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde releaser, or heavy metal.","category":"Fatty acid / emollient"}

stearic acid__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Stearic Acid","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Stearic acid is a saturated fatty acid widely used as an emulsifier, thickener, and cleansing agent in skincare, soaps, and cosmetics. It is considered low risk for the general population.","details":"It helps stabilize oil-and-water mixtures, hardens soap bars, and provides a creamy texture in lotions and cleansers. While it may be comedogenic for some acne-prone individuals, it does not belong to problematic groups like parabens, sulfates (SLS/SLES), phthalates, formaldehyde-releasing preservatives, or triclosan. Overall, it has a strong safety record in topical use.","category":"Fatty acid / emulsifier"}

myristic acid__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Myristic Acid","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Myristic acid is a fatty acid used as a cleansing agent, surfactant, and texture enhancer in personal care products. It is generally regarded as safe with low overall risk.","details":"Frequently found in facial cleansers, shaving foams, and soaps, myristic acid helps create foam and improves spreadability. It can be mildly drying or comedogenic in some people with sensitive or acne-prone skin, especially in high-foaming formulas, but it is not associated with endocrine disruption or major systemic toxicity. It is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde releaser, or heavy metal contaminant.","category":"Fatty acid / surfactant"}

petrolatum__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Petrolatum","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Petrolatum (petroleum jelly) is an occlusive moisturizer that forms a barrier on the skin to prevent water loss. Its safety depends heavily on purification quality and potential contamination with polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).","details":"Highly refined, pharmaceutical-grade petrolatum is generally considered safe and effective for dry or compromised skin, and is widely used in ointments and barrier creams. Concerns arise when petrolatum is not well refined, as impurities such as PAHs are associated with potential carcinogenic risk; regulations in many regions limit these contaminants. It can also occlude pores in some people, leading to breakouts, and may trap irritants on the skin if not used on clean skin.","category":"Occlusive emollient; petroleum-derived ingredient"}

mineral oil__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Mineral Oil","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Mineral oil is a highly refined, petroleum-derived oil used as an emollient and occlusive to soften skin and reduce moisture loss. In cosmetic grades, it is generally considered safe, but it has some controversy and can be comedogenic for certain skin types.","details":"Cosmetic- and pharmaceutical-grade mineral oil is purified to remove most harmful contaminants and is typically non-irritating and stable, making it widely used in lotions, creams, and baby products. However, like petrolatum, the main concern is potential contamination with PAHs if refinement standards are poor; stringent regulations usually control this in reputable products. It may feel heavy or greasy, can contribute to clogged pores in acne-prone individuals, and provides no additional skin nutrients beyond barrier support.","category":"Emollient and occlusive; petroleum-derived ingredient"}

carbomer__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Carbomer","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Carbomer is a synthetic polymer used to thicken, stabilize, and gel cosmetic and personal care formulations. It is generally considered low risk and well tolerated on the skin.","details":"Carbomers help control product texture, viscosity, and suspension, allowing for smooth gels and creams that spread evenly. They are inert, do not penetrate deeply into the skin, and are rarely associated with irritation or allergic reactions when properly neutralized and used at typical cosmetic concentrations. Minor sensitivity can occur in very reactive skin, but overall it is viewed as a safe formulation aid.","category":"Thickener and gelling agent"}

caprylyl glycol__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Caprylyl Glycol","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Caprylyl Glycol is a humectant and skin-conditioning agent that also boosts preservative effectiveness. It is generally well tolerated and widely used in skincare and cosmetic products.","details":"This ingredient helps attract and retain moisture in the skin, improving texture and feel of formulations while also providing mild antimicrobial support. It is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde releaser, or a common allergen for the general population. Mild irritation is possible in very sensitive or compromised skin, but overall safety data supports low risk at typical cosmetic concentrations.","category":"Humectant and emollient"}

hexylene glycol__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Hexylene Glycol","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Hexylene Glycol is a solvent and humectant used to help dissolve other ingredients and improve product texture. It is generally considered safe at typical use levels but can be irritating for some people, especially with frequent use or on sensitive skin.","details":"This ingredient improves spreadability and helps stabilize formulations, and it is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde-releasing preservative, or heavy metal. However, as a glycol solvent, it can cause mild to moderate irritation, stinging, or redness in sensitive individuals or around the eyes. Overall systemic toxicity risk is low, but due to its irritation potential in personal care products, it is best categorized as moderate risk for sensitive users.","category":"Solvent and humectant"}

phenoxyethanol__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Phenoxyethanol","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Phenoxyethanol is a widely used synthetic preservative that protects products from microbial growth. It is effective and commonly used as a paraben alternative but can cause irritation or sensitization in some individuals, especially at higher concentrations.","details":"In cosmetics and skincare, phenoxyethanol is typically used at concentrations up to 1% to prevent bacteria and mold, and it is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, or formaldehyde-releasing preservative. Regulatory agencies generally consider it safe at typical levels, but there are reports of skin and eye irritation, and rare allergic reactions, particularly in babies or very sensitive skin. Because of this irritation and sensitization potential while still being useful and relatively well studied, it is best viewed as a moderate risk ingredient in personal care products.","category":"Preservative"}

citric acid__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Citric Acid","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Citric acid is a weak organic acid used in personal care products mainly to adjust pH and act as a mild chelating agent. It is generally considered safe for most skin types.","details":"In skincare and haircare, citric acid helps maintain a stable and skin-friendly pH, which can support product effectiveness and preservation. It may cause mild irritation or stinging in people with very sensitive or compromised skin, especially at higher concentrations, but it is not associated with hormone disruption, cancer risk, or major systemic toxicity in cosmetic use. It is widely accepted by regulatory authorities as safe within typical formulation limits.","category":"pH adjuster / chelating agent"}

cetyl ethylhexanoate__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Cetyl Ethylhexanoate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Cetyl Ethylhexanoate is an emollient ester used to give products a smooth, non-greasy feel. It is generally well tolerated by skin and considered low risk for most users.","details":"This ingredient is synthesized from cetyl alcohol and 2-ethylhexanoic acid and functions mainly as a skin-conditioning and texture-enhancing agent in skincare and cosmetics. It is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde-releaser, or heavy metal, and it does not belong to the main groups of strongly drying alcohols. A small number of people with very sensitive or acne-prone skin may experience mild comedogenicity or irritation, but this is uncommon.","category":"Emollient ester"}

glyceryl stearate se__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Glyceryl Stearate Se","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Glyceryl Stearate SE is an emulsifier and emollient that helps oil and water mix and leaves skin feeling smooth. It is generally regarded as safe and non-irritating in personal care products.","details":"The “SE” means self-emulsifying, indicating it contains a small amount of added alkaline material (often sodium or potassium stearate) to help stabilize emulsions. It is derived from glycerin and stearic acid (often from vegetable oils) and is not associated with endocrine disruption, formaldehyde release, or other major cosmetic safety concerns. Most skin types tolerate it well, though extremely sensitive skin may rarely react to the alkaline components.","category":"Emulsifier and emollient"}

cetyl alcohol__personal_care__en.analysis: {"name":"Cetyl Alcohol","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Cetyl Alcohol is a fatty alcohol used as an emollient, thickener, and stabilizer in creams and lotions. Unlike simple drying alcohols, it is generally soothing and well tolerated by most skin types.","details":"This long-chain fatty alcohol helps stabilize emulsions, improve texture, and reduce moisture loss from the skin’s surface. It is distinct from low-molecular-weight alcohols like ethanol or isopropyl alcohol, which can be drying or irritating; fatty alcohols like cetyl alcohol are typically non-drying and often beneficial in moisturizers. Allergic reactions are rare, though individuals with very reactive skin or specific sensitivities to fatty alcohols may experience mild irritation.","category":"Fatty alcohol emollient and thickener"}

ground coffee beans__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Ground Coffee Beans","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Ground coffee beans are roasted coffee seeds that are milled for brewing and are generally safe for most healthy adults when consumed in moderation.","details":"The primary concern with ground coffee beans is their caffeine content, which can cause jitteriness, insomnia, increased heart rate, or digestive upset in sensitive individuals or at high intakes. Coffee can modestly raise blood pressure in some people and may aggravate certain conditions such as anxiety disorders, GERD, or heart rhythm issues. Overall, coffee also contains beneficial antioxidants and is considered safe at moderate daily consumption levels for most of the general population.","category":"Beverage ingredient"}

malted barley flour__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Malted Barley Flour","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Malted barley flour is a cereal-based flour made from sprouted and dried barley, often used to improve flavor and texture in baked goods. It is generally safe for most people but is a common gluten-containing ingredient.","details":"Because it comes from barley, malted barley flour contains gluten and is unsuitable for individuals with celiac disease or gluten intolerance, but this does not pose a risk to the general population. It can add natural sweetness, color, and aid yeast fermentation in breads and cereals. Nutritionally, it contributes some carbohydrates and small amounts of vitamins and minerals typical of cereal grains.","category":"Cereal grain ingredient"}

soybean oil__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Soybean Oil","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Soybean oil is a widely used vegetable oil extracted from soybeans and is generally safe for the general population, though it is a common allergen source for those with soy allergy. It is often used for frying, baking, and as a base in processed foods and dressings.","details":"Refined soybean oil is typically free of soy protein, so it rarely triggers allergic reactions, but sensitive individuals may still choose to avoid it. From a health perspective, it is high in polyunsaturated fats, including omega-6 fatty acids; excessive intake of omega-6 relative to omega-3 may contribute to inflammation if overall diet is unbalanced. It is not a trans fat unless it is specifically partially hydrogenated, which would then increase cardiovascular risk.","category":"Vegetable oil"}

palm kernel oil__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Palm Kernel Oil","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Palm kernel oil is a vegetable fat high in saturated fats, used for texture, shelf life, and frying stability. It is generally safe but may contribute to elevated LDL (“bad”) cholesterol when consumed in excess.","details":"Palm kernel oil is extracted from the seed of the oil palm and is more saturated than many other vegetable oils, which can negatively impact cardiovascular health if it is a frequent, major fat source in the diet. It is often used in processed and packaged foods because it is inexpensive, stable at high temperatures, and resists oxidation, which can encourage higher intake of ultra-processed foods. Environmental and sustainability concerns are also associated with palm cultivation, though these do not directly affect short-term health risk from consumption.","category":"Vegetable oil / saturated fat source"}

nonfat milk powder__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Nonfat Milk Powder","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Nonfat milk powder is dehydrated skim milk that provides protein, calcium, and other nutrients without milk fat. It is generally safe for most people but can cause reactions in individuals with milk allergy or lactose intolerance.","details":"This ingredient is made by removing most of the water and fat from milk, leaving primarily proteins (casein and whey), lactose, and minerals, making it a nutrient-dense dairy component. It is commonly used in baked goods, confectionery, and beverages to boost protein content and improve texture. For the general population it is a low-risk ingredient, though people with dairy allergy or lactose intolerance should avoid or limit it.","category":"Dairy ingredient / protein source"}

palm kernel oil and palm oil__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Palm Kernel Oil And Palm Oil","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Palm kernel oil and palm oil are plant-derived fats high in saturated fat, which can negatively impact heart health when consumed in excess. They are commonly used in processed foods for texture, stability, and long shelf life.","details":"Both palm kernel oil and palm oil are naturally free of trans fats but contain a high proportion of saturated fatty acids, which are linked to elevated LDL cholesterol and increased cardiovascular risk when regularly consumed in large amounts. They are often used as cheaper alternatives to healthier oils and may indicate a highly processed product. Environmental and sustainability concerns are also associated with palm cultivation, though this does not change direct health risk but may influence consumer choice.","category":"Fats and oils"}

cocoa powder__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Cocoa Powder","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Cocoa powder is derived from cocoa beans and provides flavor, color, and some beneficial polyphenols. In typical food amounts it is generally safe and can offer antioxidant benefits.","details":"Natural cocoa powder contains flavonoids and other bioactive compounds that may support cardiovascular health when part of an overall balanced diet and not overwhelmed by added sugar and fat. Some cocoa products can contain trace heavy metals like cadmium or lead, but levels in most regulated products are considered safe for average consumers; risk is more relevant with very high, chronic intake. People sensitive to caffeine or theobromine should be aware that cocoa naturally contains small amounts of these stimulants.","category":"Cocoa and chocolate ingredients"}

cocoa powder processed with alkali__food.analysis: {"name":"Cocoa Powder Processed With Alkali","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Cocoa powder processed with alkali, also called Dutch-processed cocoa, is treated to reduce acidity and create a milder flavor and darker color. It is generally safe for most people in typical dietary amounts.","details":"The alkalization process lowers the natural acidity of cocoa and improves solubility, but also reduces some of the native antioxidant polyphenols compared to natural cocoa. Like other cocoa ingredients, it may contain trace levels of heavy metals such as cadmium depending on source, but regulated food products are usually within safety limits for average consumption. It still contributes cocoa flavor and small amounts of caffeine and theobromine, which may matter for very sensitive individuals.","category":"Cocoa and chocolate ingredients"}

natural vanilla flavor__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Natural Vanilla Flavor","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Natural vanilla flavor is a flavoring derived from vanilla beans or other natural sources that mimic vanilla taste. It is generally recognized as safe for most people when consumed in typical food amounts.","details":"This ingredient is regulated as a natural flavor and may contain a mixture of vanilla extracts and other natural flavor compounds in an alcohol or glycerin base. While processing aids and solvents are allowed, they are used in small amounts that are not considered harmful at normal intake levels. People with very sensitive digestive systems or who avoid unspecified flavor blends may prefer products that specify pure vanilla extract instead.","category":"Flavoring"}

unbleached enriched flour__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Unbleached Enriched Flour","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Unbleached enriched flour is wheat flour that has not been chemically bleached and has vitamins and minerals added back after processing. It is safe for the general population but contains gluten and is not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten intolerance.","details":"During milling, parts of the wheat kernel and some nutrients are removed, and enrichment typically adds back iron and B vitamins such as folic acid, niacin, thiamin, and riboflavin. Although it is less processed than bleached flour, it is still a refined carbohydrate that can raise blood sugar more quickly than whole-grain flour. For most healthy individuals it is safe in moderation, but those managing blood sugar, heart health, or seeking higher fiber may prefer whole-grain alternatives.","category":"Refined grain ingredient"}
